claims.locator: p1 abstract; Methods strains; 1995 PMID7868591 reassignment
claims.paraphrase: The purified PaW1/pWW0 enzyme was called benzaldehyde dehydrogenase and attributed to xylC in 1990. Its later N-terminal reassignment to XylG must accompany reuse of these experiments.

claims.locator: Methods growth and purification; Results purification
claims.paraphrase: Benzyl-alcohol/xylene induction, Affi-Gel Blue retention and DTT handling concern this native preparation. They differ from the 1995 KT2440 pWW0-161 experiments.

claims.locator: Results molecular properties and native electrophoresis
claims.paraphrase: Apparent native/subunit masses were 126/57 kDa, supporting a dimer. A lower native-gel band showed activity after DTT treatment; this is not a universal monomer-activity rule.
Benzaldehyde oxidation yielded benzoate and NADH in a 1:1 ratio by HPLC. NADP supported less than 1% of NAD activity at 1 mM; these assays concern benzaldehyde, not HMS.
pH 9.6 and pro-R hydride transfer concern benzaldehyde assays. Do not call them HMS optimum or directly measured HMS hydride stereochemistry.

Magnesium improved storage stability modestly, while tested salts did not activate aldehyde dehydrogenase. Distinguish storage effects from catalysis and from the separate benzyl-alcohol dehydrogenase.

EDTA and phenanthroline did not inhibit in the tested conditions. Thiol reagents inhibited; mercaptoethanol restored pCMB-treated activity. These observations do not identify a particular catalytic residue.

The aldehyde dehydrogenase was not apparently inhibited by NADH. Reverse activity with benzoate/NADH was not detected under the tested conditions; ester hydrolysis was an adjacent activity of unclear physiological relevance.
